statutory_violations.broken_statute: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Section 2(46)(i) & Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 23
statutory_violations.statutory_reference: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(46): Contracts that impose unreasonable conditions or unilateral automatic continuations without explicit opt-in consent are classified as Unfair Contracts and are unenforceable.
statutory_violations.impact: requires 45-day advance cancellation to avoid lock-in
statutory_violations.remedy:
Re: Objection to Mandatory Auto-Renewal Mechanism

Dear Sir/Madam,

I have reviewed Clause 11 of the revised draft which introduces an automatic renewal of the 11-month term unless 45 days advance notice is served.

Under Section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, automatic renewal clauses that impose deemed consent and financial penalties for exit constitute unfair contract terms. Any renewal of tenancy or engagement must occur through explicit mutual consent executed in writing.

I request that Clause 11 be modified to state that renewal shall occur strictly upon express mutual written agreement between the parties at least 30 days before expiry.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
statutory_violations.forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) or Jurisdictional Civil / Rent Court

statutory_violations.statutory_reference: Model Tenancy Act, 2021, Section 11: Security deposit for residential premises shall not exceed two months' rent and must be refunded to the tenant within one month of vacating after agreed deductions.
statutory_violations.violation_type: Direct Statutory Breach / Unfair Contract Term
statutory_violations.impact: extends your obligation / wait by 60 days
statutory_violations.remedy:
Re: Objection to Unlawful Extension of Security Deposit Refund Window

Dear Landlord,

I am in receipt of the revised Tenancy Agreement. Clause 5 seeks to extend the refund timeline for my security deposit to 90 days.

Please note that under Section 11 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, the statutory deadline for refunding the security deposit after vacant possession is strictly 30 days (one month). Furthermore, imposing an unreasonable 90-day retention constitutes an 'Unfair Contract' under Section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

I request you to amend this clause back to the statutory limit of 30 days prior to execution. Failing this, I reserve the right to report this deviation to the jurisdictional Rent Authority under Section 30 of the Model Tenancy Act.

Yours sincerely,
[Tenant Name]
statutory_violations.forum: Rent Authority / Rent Court under Section 30 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (or District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission)

statutory_violations.statutory_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 23: An agreement the terms of which are opposed to public policy or force one party to indemnify another against their own negligence is void ab initio.
statutory_violations.violation_type: Unconscionable Indemnity Clause / Void Under Sec 23
statutory_violations.impact: increases your personal financial exposure (amount not specified in clause)
statutory_violations.remedy:
Re: Objection to Unilateral Indemnity Clause

Dear Sir/Madam,

Clause 8 requires me to indemnify and hold harmless the counterparty from all losses, claims, and injuries. Under settled Indian jurisprudence (Central Inland Water Transport Corp principle) and Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, blanket exculpatory clauses excluding one party's liability for structural defects or negligence are void as opposed to public policy.

Please amend the clause to state that each party remains liable for its own acts, omissions, or gross negligence.

Regards,
[Your Name]
statutory_violations.forum: Civil Court / District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission

statutory_violations.statutory_reference: Model Tenancy Act, 2021, Section 9 & 10: Revision of rent shall be in accordance with terms agreed in the tenancy agreement. Notice of revision must be given at least three months before revision takes effect.
statutory_violations.remedy:
Re: Notice of Irregular Rent Revision

Dear Landlord,

The proposed rent increase from ₹28,000 to ₹32,000 (~14.3%) exceeds agreed terms and was not accompanied by the mandatory 3 months written notice required under Section 10 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021.

I request that rent revision be capped at the customary 5-7% rate and effective only after the statutory 3-month notice period.

Sincerely,
[Tenant Name]
statutory_violations.forum: Rent Authority under Section 10 of Model Tenancy Act, 2021

statutory_violations.broken_statute: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 62 & Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Section 2(46)(vi)
statutory_violations.statutory_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 62 requires mutual consensus ad idem for novation or variation of contract. Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(46)(vi) declares unilateral contract modifications as Unfair Contracts.
statutory_violations.violation_type: Unfair Contract Term / Void Variation Clause
statutory_violations.impact: terms may change without your affirmative consent
statutory_violations.remedy:
Re: Rejection of Unilateral Modification Clause

Dear Sir/Madam,

Clause 12 reserves the right to amend terms at sole discretion via email. Under Section 62 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and Section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, contract variations without bilateral consent are void.

Please replace this with: 'No amendment or variation of this Agreement shall be valid unless agreed to in writing and signed by both parties.'

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

statutory_violations.broken_statute: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 28 & Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
statutory_violations.statutory_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 28: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings are void. The Supreme Court in Vidya Drolia (2020) affirmed that landlord-tenant disputes governed by special tenancy statutes are non-arbitrable.
statutory_violations.impact: limits court options — dispute path changes
statutory_violations.remedy:
Re: Objection to Private Arbitration Clause in Tenancy

Dear Landlord,

Clause 10 introduces mandatory private arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. As settled by the Supreme Court of India in Vidya Drolia (2020), tenancy disputes governed by statutory rent frameworks are non-arbitrable and fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the designated Rent Authority / Civil Courts.

Please remove the private arbitration clause and restore standard jurisdictional recourse to local courts / Rent Authorities.

Sincerely,
[Tenant Name]
statutory_violations.forum: Jurisdictional Rent Authority / Civil Court (Private arbitration can be challenged under Section 11/16 of Arbitration Act)

statutory_violations.broken_statute: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — Section 106 & Model Tenancy Act, 2021 — Section 21
statutory_violations.statutory_reference: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Section 106 provides 15 days notice for monthly residential leases unless reasonably agreed. MTA Section 21 provides termination mechanisms on agreed terms without punitive double lock-ins.
statutory_violations.impact: extends your obligation / wait by 30 days
statutory_violations.remedy:
Re: Revision of Notice Period to 30 Days

Dear Landlord,

I note that the revised draft increases notice period from 30 to 60 days and adds lock-in penalties. Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, liquidated damages must reflect actual reasonable loss rather than a penalty.

I propose maintaining the 30-day notice period as agreed in our initial tenancy.

Regards,
[Tenant Name]
